# A fixed-dimensional sub-half hyperplane obstruction to the coarse center bridge

Here hyperplanes are in the distinguished fine coordinate alone, as in the definition of \(\eta\) in fine-hyperplane-nonconcentration-forces-component-recovery.md. They are not all hyperplanes in the combined coarse and fine integer coordinates.

The ten-point diamond source gives an exact obstruction with \(\eta=1/9<1/2\), fixed \(k=3,r=1,s\ge2\), a full-dimensional body, and equality of the body with the convex hull of its fine mixed source. This strengthens the three-slice example that only disproves a density inference.

## 1. An integral shear of the audited diamond body

Use candidate a2bca99efffd5fb9, with coordinates \((z,u,x)\in\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^s\), and apply
\[
       (z,u,x)\longmapsto
       (z,u'=u+100z_1+10z_2+z_3,x).                     \tag{1}
\]
This invertible integral shear has determinant one and acts identically on \(x\). It preserves both the coarse rule \(z\in\mathbb Z^3\) and the fine rule \((z,u)\in\mathbb Z^4\), because its offset is integer at every coarse base. It maps ambient closed halfspaces bijectively to closed halfspaces. Full dimension, convexity, and equality with the hull of the actual fine mixed set are preserved.

Every coarse intrinsic fiber is one copy of the same \(s\)-simplex \(K\) at a fixed height. The shear only translates that height and preserves its intrinsic \(H_s\) measure. Every fine fiber is likewise unchanged.

The positive fine bases, with the archived indices, acquire these heights:

| Index | \(z\) | Old \(u\) | New \(u'\) |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| \(0\) | \((0,0,1)\) | \(1\) | \(2\) |
| \(1\) | \((1,0,0)\) | \(1\) | \(101\) |
| \(3\) | \((1,0,2)\) | \(0\) | \(102\) |
| \(4\) | \((1,1,0)\) | \(0\) | \(110\) |
| \(5\) | \((1,1,1)\) | \(0\) | \(111\) |
| \(6\) | \((2,0,1)\) | \(0\) | \(201\) |
| \(7\) | \((2,1,0)\) | \(0\) | \(210\) |
| \(8\) | \((2,1,1)\) | \(0\) | \(211\) |
| \(10\) | \((2,2,0)\) | \(0\) | \(220\) |

These levels are pairwise distinct and all nine fibers have equal mass. An affine hyperplane in the one-dimensional fine space is one level, so its largest mass fraction is exactly \(1/9\). The additional coarse-only base \(p_2=(1,0,1)\) has height \(203/2\), still nonintegral, and no fine mass.

## 2. Exact failure of the naive rank-drop center bound

The audited all-cap proofs and shear invariance give
\[
       D_{\rm coarse}=\frac{\Gamma_s}{2},
       \qquad D_{\rm fine}=\frac{\Gamma_s}{9}.            \tag{2}
\]
These are maxima over every actual candidate point, not prescribed selectors. All upper-cover caps, lower-bound centers, and their containing halfspaces are carried through (1).

The coarse source has intrinsic dimension \(s\), although its continuous ambient dimension is \(s+1\); its full coarse \((s+1)\)-volume is zero. The fine source has intrinsic dimension \(s\) and nine positive fibers. Those are the normalizations in (2).

For every fixed \(s\ge2\),
\[
                   \frac{\Gamma_s}{9}
                         <\frac{\Gamma_{s+1}}8.         \tag{3}
\]
Indeed \((\log\Gamma_t)''=1/[t(t+1)^2]>0\), so \(\Gamma_{s+1}/\Gamma_s>8/9\) for \(s\ge2\). Thus no fine center satisfies the naive coarse-rank-three target on the right of (3), despite \(\eta=1/9\), the full ambient body, and the exact-fine-hull condition.

This does not contradict the true fine OC target \(\Gamma_s/16\), which is smaller than (2). It also does not contradict recovery when \(\eta_l\to0\): this constant sequence has \(\eta_l=1/9\). Nor does it satisfy nonconcentration on every combined integer-base hyperplane; the old seven-point height-zero plane is carried to an oblique combined-base hyperplane.

The exact arithmetic is checked by verify_subhalf_fine_hyperplane_bridge_obstruction.py. Its geometric and all-cap dependencies are precisely the already audited diamond construction.
